title: Zero Childhood Cancer (ZERO)
tagline: Australia’s national precision-medicine program for children with cancer — led from Randwick
partners: Kids Cancer Centre, Sydney Children’s Hospital Randwick

impact.evidence_note: Nature Medicine 2024 high-risk cohort; national standard-of-care expansion

milestones.label: Clinical challenge
milestones.detail: High-risk childhood cancers had limited treatment options and poor survival. Clinicians needed tumour molecular drivers to guide personalised therapy.

milestones.label: Precinct partnership
milestones.detail: Children’s Cancer Institute joined with the Kids Cancer Centre at Sydney Children’s Hospital, Randwick, to launch ZERO — later expanded with UNSW and national hospital partners.

milestones.label: National trial
milestones.detail: First national precision-medicine trial enrolled children with high-risk cancers across Australia’s children’s hospitals, generating molecular reports for treating oncologists.

milestones.label: Clinical validation
milestones.detail: Nature Medicine study of 384 high-risk patients: 55% who received personalised treatment achieved remission or ≥6-month disease stability; 2-year progression-free survival more than doubled vs standard care (26% vs 12%).

milestones.label: National scale-up
milestones.detail: From late 2023 ZERO became available to every Australian child (0–18) with cancer. Further Commonwealth investment ($112.6M announced 2025) extends access toward young adults with paediatric-type cancers (~1,300 people/year).

title: Keeping the Body in Mind (KBIM)
tagline: Embedding lifestyle care in early psychosis services to prevent antipsychotic-related weight gain
partners: South Eastern Sydney Local Health District

impact.evidence_note: Pilot + routine-care audit across SESLHD early psychosis services (2015–2019)

impact_metrics.label: Mean weight gain vs usual care (pilot)

milestones.label: Clinical challenge
milestones.detail: Antipsychotic treatment in first-episode psychosis often triggers rapid cardiometabolic harm — historically ~75–80% of youth experienced clinically significant weight gain within weeks.

milestones.label: Precinct collaboration
milestones.detail: SESLHD clinicians and UNSW researchers embedded dietitians, exercise physiologists and life-skills support in early psychosis care — later amplified through the Mindgardens Alliance (UNSW, NeuRA, Black Dog Institute, SESLHD).

milestones.label: Pilot evidence
milestones.detail: 12-week KBIM pilot limited mean weight gain to ~1.8 kg vs ~7.8 kg under usual care; clinically significant weight gain fell to 13% vs 75% at the control site.

milestones.label: Routine care scale-up
milestones.detail: Rolled out across three SESLHD early psychosis services. Audit of 182 participants (134 with follow-up): mean +1.5 kg; 81% avoided clinically significant weight gain — matching pilot results in real-world care.

milestones.label: Translational impact
milestones.detail: KBIM informed policy and practice nationally and internationally. Mindgardens’ KBIM program received the Angelo Cocchi Translational Impact Award (IEPA, Berlin) for translating research into systemic mental-health reform.

title: Minderoo Children’s Comprehensive Cancer Centre
tagline: Bench-to-bedside children’s cancer care under one roof at the Randwick campus

impact.evidence_note: Capital and partnership delivery of Australia’s first Children’s Comprehensive Cancer Centre at RHIP

milestones.label: System challenge
milestones.detail: Children’s cancer research and care were strong at Randwick but split across sites — slowing the path from discovery to bedside treatment.

milestones.label: Precinct partnership
milestones.detail: Built on decades of collaboration between Children’s Cancer Institute, the Kids Cancer Centre (SCH Randwick) and UNSW — the same partnership behind ZERO.

milestones.label: Campus redevelopment
milestones.detail: Sydney Children’s Hospital Stage 1 and the Minderoo Children’s Comprehensive Cancer Centre delivered as one $658M facility (Bilima Building), linking clinical care with the adjacent UNSW Health Translation Hub.

milestones.label: Integrated care & research
milestones.detail: Researchers, clinicians and educators work side-by-side so discoveries can move faster to nearby hospital beds — extending the ZERO precision-medicine model into a dedicated comprehensive cancer centre.

milestones.label: Official opening
milestones.detail: Australia’s first Children’s Comprehensive Cancer Centre opened at Randwick with federal and NSW government support plus philanthropy from Minderoo Foundation, CCI, SCH Foundation and UNSW — a flagship RHIP translation outcome.
